what_it_does: This paper describes a wireless communication chip that must simultaneously receive weak signals cleanly, transmit strong signals efficiently, and prevent its own transmission from drowning out incoming signals—three conflicting design goals needed for 5G, satellite communications, and advanced radio systems. The team built a single integrated circuit in a 65 nanometer CMOS process (an older, proven manufacturing technology) that operates across a wide frequency range (17.7 to 29.5 GHz, in the millimeter-wave band where 5G and satellite radios operate). By carefully routing signals and using tunable components, they achieved industry-leading low noise in receiving, high power in transmitting, and strong isolation between transmit and receive paths in the same device.
